Rural credit in IFAD-financed projects in Yemen, 1993 to 2010: an evaluation by IFAD's Independent Office of Evaluation (2011)

Report an error

01What does this evidence establish?

An evaluation of IFAD's Yemen programme from 1993 to 2010 by IFAD's Independent Office of Evaluation (2011) reports, on the evaluation team's estimates from the information held by the Cooperative and Agriculture Credit Bank (CACB), that in the completed projects credit lines disbursed US$4.165 million, 31% of the US$13.37 million provided, to 3,723 clients, 6% of the 58,867 planned; repayment rates ranged from 31% to 64%. In one project area, Raymah, fewer than 1% of the farmers in the project area received financing during the project (assuming 48,000 households in the area), and in the Southern Governorates the rural finance component was, in the evaluators' words, not really implemented at all. The evaluation reports that poor households were said to be reluctant to borrow from the CACB, the government bank the projects depended on, because of its collateral requirements, high transaction costs and lengthy approval procedures and a reluctance to deal with an institution seen as charging interest contrary to Islamic precepts; that women, who did not generally own land, had little access to its credit, as was also true of sharecroppers; and that two of the branches IFAD helped the CACB build, at Al-Jabeen in Raymah and Sayhut in Al-Mahara, were not located near commercial centres.

02What does it measure?

Findings on rural finance in IFAD-financed projects in Yemen from 1993 to 2010, from the Country Programme Evaluation by IFAD's Independent Office of Evaluation (2011).

03Who or what does it apply to?

IFAD-financed projects in Yemen and their project areas; the lending figures cover the completed projects.

04How current is it?

The evaluation is dated 6 October 2011 and covers 1993 to 2010 (checked on 11 October 2026). It should not be read as describing a later period.

05What this evidence does not establish

These are historical findings for specific project areas before the conflict; they are not a measure of rural access to finance today, and the delivery channels have since changed.

Limits of the measure

The lending figures are the evaluators' estimates for the completed projects, not audited accounts, and the reasons for low uptake are views the evaluation reports, drawn from project documents and discussions with potential clients.

07Method and verification detail

Detail for reproducing or challenging this record without changing what it means.

How was it produced?

Read from the evaluation (document EC 2011/69/W.P.4/Rev.1, dated 6 October 2011, distribution Public; its title page is dated 23 September 2011): paragraphs 176 and 177 (printed p. 40) for the lending, outreach and repayment figures, which footnote 101 says the evaluation team estimated from the latest information available with the CACB; paragraphs 138 to 140 (printed p. 33) for the reasons reported; paragraphs 9 and 10 (printed p. 3) for the period covered. In Raymah the share of farmers financed uses the farmers in the project area (footnote 102 assumes 48,000 households), while the project's 10% indicator refers to landowning farmers, so the two are not one measure and are not set against each other here.

When does this record change?
